# Appeal of Denial — Total Ankle Replacement (CPT 27702)

**RE: Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-14**
**Member:** Quinn Iverson
**Member ID:** W154693844
**Reference Number:** POC-E14E3A00BC-47205
**Plan:** Wellpoint (Commercial/ACA), New Jersey
**Governing Policy:** *Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Small Joint Surgery (Carelon)*, effective 11/05/2023 — https://files.providernews.anthem.com/2519/PDF-Small-Joint-Surgery-2023-11-05.pdf

Dear Wellpoint Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for a total ankle replacement (CPT 27702), which my surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented is medically necessary. The denial notice states that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I am asking the plan to reconsider this decision because my medical records show that I have already met the plan's own published criteria for this surgery.

## The Plan's Own Criteria and My Records

The governing policy states:

> "ankle arthroplasty is considered medically necessary in skeletally mature patients when ALL of the following criteria are met:"

> "• Radiographic confirmation of advanced/end-stage arthritis of the tibiotalar joint • Significant pain and functional impairment due to arthritis of the ankle persist after at least 3 months of supervised conservative management • Documentation of adequate lower extremity vascular perfusion (e.g., strong, palpable pedal pulses) • Device is FDA approved Total ankle arthroplasty may also be indicated for revision of failed previous reconstructions where sufficient bone stock and soft tissue integrity are present."

Here is how my records address each part of this criteria:

**1. Radiographic confirmation of advanced/end-stage arthritis of the tibiotalar joint.**
My weight-bearing ankle radiographs from 2026-07-17 showed tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts.

**2. Significant pain and functional impairment persisting after at least 3 months of supervised conservative management.**
I completed 16 weeks (2026-03-24 to 2026-07-14) of supervised physical therapy focused on ankle strengthening and balance, with 20 visits documented in my physical therapy discharge note. This is longer than the 3-month period the policy describes. I also used NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief, and had a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-05 that gave only 3 weeks of partial relief. Despite all of this, I have had 18 months of progressive pain, unrelieved by rest. I currently walk with an antalgic gait and am limited to two blocks, and my exam showed positive provocative testing and range of motion limited by pain.

The policy also states:

> "For the purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated ≥ 4 on the VAS scale and associated with difficulty performing at least 2 impacted daily activities, such as walking and wearing reasonable shoes."

My records document difficulty with walking (limited to two blocks with an antalgic gait). [A numeric VAS pain score and documentation of a second impacted daily activity, if available in the chart, should be added here to confirm this element directly.]

**3. Documentation of adequate lower extremity vascular perfusion.**
[This information — such as documentation of strong, palpable pedal pulses — should be confirmed from the physical exam notes and added here if available.]

**4. Device is FDA approved.**
[The specific device to be used and confirmation of its FDA approval status should be provided by my surgeon's office if not already included in the submitted records.]

## Why This Matters

The policy also states that Carelon's review process:

> "applies objective and evidence-based criteria, and takes individual circumstances and the local delivery system into account when determining the medical appropriateness of health care services."

and that these criteria:

> "are designed to guide both providers and reviewers to the most appropriate services based on a patient's unique circumstances."

My records show a conservative care trial — physical therapy, medication, and injection — that lasted well beyond the 3-month period referenced in the plan's own criteria, along with radiographic findings the plan's policy identifies as qualifying evidence. I am asking the plan to review these records again against its own published criteria, quoted above, and to reconsider the determination.

## Request

I am requesting that Wellpoint reverse the denial of CPT 27702 and approve the total ankle replacement recommended by my surgeon, Dr. Okafor. I have attached or will have my provider's office submit any supporting documentation needed to complete the vascular perfusion and device information referenced above.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-10. I will send this appeal to the address listed on my denial letter, and I understand I can also submit it online at anthem.com, through the Sydney Health app, or by calling the number on the back of my member ID card.

Thank you for reconsidering my case.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Quinn Iverson
Member ID: W154693844
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Date]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*

Conservative management offered by the provider or other health professionals for this condition(s) should include footwear modification and/or padding/accommodative devices (e.g., foot orthosis) AND at least one of the following complementary strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and improve function:

• Activity modification • Anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics • Corticosteroid injection(s) • Debridement of associated hyperkeratotic lesions, such as corns or calluses Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate.
